trial_title: Coated or Chewable Aspirin and a Hybrid Strategy to Mitigate Adverse Effects of Air Pollution in Stable Atherosclerotic Disease
brief_summary: Although both enteric-coated and plain formulations of aspirin are being used commonly, there are no high-quality comparisons between these formulations with respect to clinical efficacy outcomes in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases (ASCVD). Air pollution is also a major contributor to the excess risk of cardiovascular events in many regions of the world. eligibility_table.criterion: Adult patients (≥18 years) with documented ASCVD defined as at least one of the following:
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is an adult male, meeting the age criterion.

eligibility_table.criterion: Coronary artery disease (CAD):
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has documented coronary artery disease (CAD) as part of his conditions.

eligibility_table.criterion: Previous or recent documented type I myocardial infarction *(if not specified, will be assumed as type I)
eligibility_table.justification: There is no documented history of a type I myocardial infarction in the patient's profile.

eligibility_table.criterion: History of coronary revascularization (percutaneous coronary intervention or coronary artery bypass graft surgery)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of coronary revascularization (CABG).

eligibility_table.justification: There is no specific documentation of obstructive CAD (>50% stenosis) via imaging in the provided history.

eligibility_table.criterion: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD):
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has moderate to severe peripheral vascular disease (PVD), which qualifies as peripheral arterial disease (PAD).

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information regarding a previous acute ischemic limb event in the patient's history.

eligibility_table.criterion: History of ulcer or lower extremities amputation due to ASCVD.

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a history of gastrointestinal ulcers or undergone a lower extremity amputation due to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)?

eligibility_table.criterion: Carotid arterial diseases:
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant bilateral carotid artery disease, which qualifies under carotid arterial diseases.

eligibility_table.criterion: Being within 72 days of acute/unstable atherosclerotic cardiovascular events (acute myocardial infarction, acute limb event, and acute ischemic stroke), or within 72 hours of revascularization.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has not experienced any acute/unstable cardiovascular events within the specified time frame.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients receiving triple antithrombotic therapy

eligibility_table.criterion: History of intracranial hemorrhage within the past 30 days
eligibility_table.justification: There is no documented history of intracranial hemorrhage within the past 30 days.

eligibility_table.criterion: End-stage kidney disease with estimated creatinine clearance < 15 mL/min, or undergoing hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication of end-stage kidney disease or dialysis treatment.

eligibility_table.criterion: Known comorbidities associated with poor prognosis (e.g., metastatic cancer) in conjunction with an estimated life expectancy of less than one year according to the treating clinician
eligibility_table.justification: The patient does not have known comorbidities associated with poor prognosis that would affect life expectancy.

eligibility_table.justification: While the patient has a history of ischemic stroke, there is no indication that it was treated with low-dose aspirin, which is a requirement for this criterion.
